sentences.t: श्रीभगवानुवाच
sentences.tr: śrībhagavān uvāca
sentences.l: The Blessed Lord said

morph.gloss: holy, glorious (honorific prefix)
the Blessed One, the Lord — Kṛṣṇa's title as speaker (nom. sg. bhagavān; -n + u- written joined)
to speak (uvāca: perfect 3rd sg. 'said')

sentences.t:
इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे ।
ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥
sentences.tr:
idam tu te guhyatamam pravakṣyāmi anasūyave |
jñānam vijñāna-sahitam yat jñātvā mokṣyase aśubhāt ||

morph.gloss: this (nom./acc. sg. neut., referring forward to jñānam of the second line)
but
you (te: enclitic dat. sg. 'to you')
most secret, superlative of guhya (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with idam)
to declare, proclaim (pravakṣyāmi: future 1st sg. 'I shall declare'; -i + a- → -y a-)
free from malice, uncensorious, not carping (anasūyave: dat. sg. masc., addressed to Arjuna)
knowledge (nom./acc. sg. neut., in apposition to idam, object of pravakṣyāmi)
realization, discriminative/experiential knowledge (first compound member)
accompanied by, combined with (vijñāna-sahita: 'combined with realization', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with jñānam)
which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, referring to jñānam; -t + j- → -j jñ-, assimilation)
to know (jñātvā: gerund 'having known')
to release, free (mokṣyase: future middle 2nd sg. 'you shall be released'; -e + a- → -e with avagraha)
inauspicious, evil (aśubhāt: abl. sg. neut., 'from evil')

sentences.l: This, but, to-you, the-most-secret, I-shall-declare, to-one-free-of-malice: knowledge combined-with-realization, which having-known you-shall-be-released from-evil.
sentences.i: To you, who bear me no ill will, I shall declare this most secret thing: knowledge joined with direct realization, knowing which you shall be freed from evil.
sentences.n: This opens the chapter's title-teaching (rāja-vidyā, rāja-guhyam, named at verse 2) with a direct address: anasūyave, 'to one free of malice/envy, uncensorious', names Arjuna as a fit recipient because he does not carp or cavil at what he is told. Vijñāna-sahitam, 'combined with vijñāna [realization, experiential knowledge]', distinguishes the jñāna about to be taught from mere theoretical knowledge. Sandhi: यज्ज्ञात्वा packs yat + jñātvā (-t + j- → -j jñ-, assimilation); मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् is mokṣyase + aśubhāt (avagraha).

sentences.t:
राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् ।
प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम् ॥
sentences.tr:
rāja-vidyā rāja-guhyam pavitram idam uttamam |
pratyakṣa-avagamam dharmyam su-sukham kartum avyayam ||

morph.gloss: king, royal (first compound member)
knowledge, science (rāja-vidyā: 'royal knowledge, the king of sciences', nom. sg. fem., in apposition to the jñāna of verse 1)
king, royal (first compound member)
secret (rāja-guhya: 'royal secret, the king of secrets', nom. sg. neut.)
pure, purifying (nom. sg. neut.; joined before i-, no change)
this (nom. sg. neut., referring to the jñāna of verse 1; joined before u-, no change)
highest, supreme (nom. sg. neut.)
directly perceptible, evident to the senses (first compound member)
comprehension, understanding (pratyakṣa-avagama: 'directly comprehensible, verifiable by one's own experience', nom. sg. neut.; a + a → ā)
conformable to dharma, righteous (nom. sg. neut.)
good, easy (prefix)
ease, happiness (su-sukha: 'very easy', nom. sg. neut.)
to do, perform (kartum: infinitive 'to do, to practice', governed by sukham, 'easy to do')
imperishable, undiminishing (nom. sg. neut.; joined before a-, no change)

sentences.l: Royal-knowledge, royal-secret, pure, this, supreme, directly-comprehensible, dharma-conforming, very-easy to-do, imperishable.
sentences.i: It is royal knowledge, the royal secret, pure and supreme, verifiable by direct experience, in keeping with dharma, very easy to practice, and imperishable.
sentences.n: A cascade of nominal epithets, all describing the jñāna announced in verse 1 (rāja-vidyā is feminine, agreeing with vidyā's own inherent gender, while the rest are neuter, agreeing with jñānam — a normal mismatch when nouns and adjectives are simply juxtaposed in apposition rather than made to agree). Pratyakṣa-avagamam, 'directly comprehensible', claims this knowledge is verified by one's own experience, not only by scriptural authority. Sandhi: प्रत्यक्षावगमं is pratyakṣa + avagamam (a+a→ā); पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् and कर्तुमव्ययम् both show a final -m simply written joined before a following vowel, with no phonetic change (pavitram+idam+uttamam, kartum+avyayam).

sentences.t:
अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप ।
अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि ॥
sentences.tr:
a-śraddadhānāḥ puruṣāḥ dharmasya asya parantapa |
a-prāpya mām nivartante mṛtyu-saṃsāra-vartmani ||

morph.gloss: to have faith (śraddadhāna: present participle negated by a-, 'not having faith, faithless', nom. pl. masc.)
man, person (nom. pl. masc., subject; visarga dropped before the voiced dh- of dharmasya, the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ)
dharma (dharmasya: gen. sg., 'of this dharma')
this (asya: gen. sg. neut.; dharmasya + asya: a + a → ā)
'scorcher of the foe', an epithet of Arjuna (vocative)
to fail to attain, not obtain (aprāpya: gerund 'not having attained')
I (acc. sg. 'me')
to turn back, return (present middle 3rd pl.)
death (first compound member)
transmigration, the cycle of rebirth (second member)
path, road (mṛtyu-saṃsāra-vartman: 'the path of death and transmigration', loc. sg.)

sentences.l: Faithless men, of-this dharma, O scorcher-of-the-foe, not-attaining me, return on-the-path of-death-and-transmigration.
sentences.i: Men who lack faith in this dharma, Parantapa, fail to reach me and return instead to the path of death and rebirth.
sentences.n: A warning that closes the opening address: those without śraddhā, 'faith', in this dharma cannot attain Kṛṣṇa and remain on the path of mṛtyu-saṃsāra, 'death and transmigration'. Parantapa, 'scorcher of the foe', an epithet of Arjuna. Sandhi: पुरुषा is puruṣāḥ with its visarga simply dropped (not changed to -o) before the voiced dh- of dharmasya, because the stem vowel is ā (long), not a (short) — a distinction that recurs often in this chapter: -aḥ (short a) before a voiced consonant becomes -o, but -āḥ (long ā) before a voiced consonant just loses the visarga; धर्मस्यास्य packs dharmasya + asya (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना ।
मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः ॥
sentences.tr:
mayā tatam idam sarvam jagat avyakta-mūrtinā |
mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni na ca aham teṣu avasthitaḥ ||

morph.gloss: I (instr. sg. 'by me')
to stretch, extend, pervade (tata: past participle 'pervaded, extended', nom. sg. neut.)
this (nom. sg. neut.; joined before i-, no change)
all (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with jagat)
the world (nom. sg. neut., subject, in apposition to idam sarvam; -t + a- → -d a-)
unmanifest (first compound member)
form, embodiment (avyakta-mūrti: 'of unmanifest form', instr. sg., agreeing with mayā)
me (stem form, first compound member)
situated, resting (mat-stha: 'situated in me', nom. pl. neut., agreeing with sarva-bhūtāni)
all (first compound member)
being (sarva-bhūta: 'all beings', nom. pl. neut., subject)
not
and
I (nom. sg., subject; ca + aham: a + a → ā)
those/them (teṣu: loc. pl. neut. 'among them')
to be situated, established (avasthitaḥ: past participle, nom. sg. masc., predicate; teṣu + a- → teṣv a-, yaṇ sandhi u + a → va)

sentences.l: By-me pervaded, this, all, the-world, unmanifest-in-form; in-me-resting all-beings, and-not I in-them established.
sentences.i: By me, in my unmanifest form, this whole world is pervaded; all beings rest in me, but I am not established in them.
sentences.n: The chapter's first statement of the paradox worked out through verse 10: all things rest in Kṛṣṇa (mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni) even as he, in his unmanifest form (avyakta-mūrti), remains untouched by them (na ca aham teṣu avasthitaḥ). Sandhi: ततमिदं is tatam+idam, joined; जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना is jagat+avyakta-mūrtinā (-t+a-→-d a-); चाहं is ca+aham (a+a→ā); तेष्ववस्थितः is teṣu+avasthitaḥ (yaṇ sandhi, u+a→va).

sentences.t:
न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ।
भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः ॥
sentences.tr:
na ca mat-sthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogam aiśvaram |
bhūta-bhṛt na ca bhūta-sthaḥ mama ātmā bhūta-bhāvanaḥ ||

morph.gloss: not
and
me (stem form, first compound member)
situated (mat-stha: 'situated in me', nom. pl. neut., repeated from verse 4)
being (nom. pl. neut., subject)
to see (paśya: imperative 2nd sg. 'behold!')
I (me: gen. sg. enclitic 'my')
yoga, kept untranslated (acc. sg., object of paśya)
lordly, majestic, of a sovereign lord (from īśvara; acc. sg. neut., agreeing with yogam; joined before ai-, no change)
being (first compound member)
to bear, sustain (bhṛt: agent noun 'bearer, sustainer', bhūta-bhṛt: 'sustainer of beings', nom. sg.; -t + n- → -n n-, assimilation)
not
and
being (first compound member)
situated, abiding (bhūta-stha: 'abiding in beings', nom. sg., negated by the preceding na; -aḥ before m- → -o)
I (mama: gen. sg. 'my'; mama + ātmā: a + ā → ā)
self, soul (nom. sg., subject)
being (first compound member)
to be, come into existence (causative bhāvayati; bhāvana: 'that which causes to be, the source of being', bhūta-bhāvana: 'the source of beings' existence', nom. sg., predicate)

sentences.l: And-not in-me-resting [are] the-beings — behold my lordly yoga! Sustainer-of-beings, and-not abiding-in-beings, [is] my self, the-source-of-beings'-existence.
sentences.i: And yet the beings do not really rest in me — behold this power of mine, my lordly yoga! My self sustains all beings and yet does not abide within them; it is the very source from which beings come to exist.
sentences.n: This deepens verse 4's paradox to the point of open contradiction — beings both do (v.4) and do not (v.5) rest in Kṛṣṇa — and names it explicitly as yogam aiśvaram, 'a lordly power', not to be resolved by ordinary logic. Bhūta-bhṛt, 'sustainer of beings', and bhūta-stha, 'abiding in beings' (here negated), are set against each other exactly as mat-sthāni and na avasthitaḥ were in verse 4. Sandhi: योगमैश्वरम् is yogam+aiśvaram, joined; भूतभृन्न packs bhūta-bhṛt+na (-t+n-→-nn-, assimilation); भूतस्थो is bhūta-sthaḥ, -aḥ before m- → -o; ममात्मा is mama+ātmā (a+ā→ā).

sentences.t:
यथाकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् ।
तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय ॥
sentences.tr:
yathā ākāśa-sthitaḥ nityam vāyuḥ sarvatra-gaḥ mahān |
tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni mat-sthāni iti upadhāraya ||

morph.gloss: as, just as (yathā + ākāśa: ā + ā → ā, written joined)
space, ether (first compound member)
situated, abiding (ākāśa-sthita: 'situated in space', nom. sg. masc., agreeing with vāyuḥ; -aḥ before n- → -o)
always, constantly (adverb)
wind, air (nom. sg., subject)
everywhere (first compound member/adverb)
going (sarvatra-ga: 'going everywhere, all-pervading', nom. sg.; -aḥ before m- → -o)
great (mahān: nom. sg. masc.)
so, likewise
all (nom. pl. neut., agreeing with bhūtāni)
being (nom. pl. neut., subject)
me (stem form, first compound member)
situated (mat-stha: 'situated in me', nom. pl. neut., predicate)
thus, closing the predication (sthāni + iti: i + i → ī)
to hold up, grasp, understand (upadhāraya: causative imperative 2nd sg. 'understand!, know!'; iti + upadhāraya: i + u → yu)

sentences.l: As space-abiding, always, the-wind, everywhere-going, great, so all beings in-me-resting — thus understand.
sentences.i: Just as the wind, great and moving everywhere, always abides in space, so understand that all beings abide in me.
sentences.n: A simile resolving the paradox of verses 4-5: as the vāyu, 'wind', is wholly contained within ākāśa, 'space', yet space is not thereby confined to or exhausted by the wind, so all beings rest in Kṛṣṇa without limiting or containing him. Mat-sthāni, 'resting in me', repeats verse 4's key phrase. Sandhi: यथाकाशस्थितो packs yathā+ākāśa-sthitaḥ (ā+ā→ā, then -aḥ before n-→-o); सर्वत्रगो is sarvatra-gaḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o; मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय packs mat-sthāni+iti (i+i→ī) +upadhāraya (i+u→yu).

sentences.t:
सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम् ।
कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम् ॥
sentences.tr:
sarva-bhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtim yānti māmikām |
kalpa-kṣaye punaḥ tāni kalpa-ādau visṛjāmi aham ||

morph.gloss: all (first compound member)
being (sarva-bhūta: 'all beings', nom. pl. neut., subject)
'son of Kuntī', Arjuna (vocative)
nature, primal matter (acc. sg. fem., object of yānti)
to go (present 3rd pl.)
my, mine (māmikām: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with prakṛtim, 'my own')
a cosmic cycle, aeon (first compound member)
destruction, dissolution, ending (kalpa-kṣaya: 'the dissolution of the aeon', loc. sg.)
again (punaḥ: -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
them (tāni: acc. pl. neut., object of visṛjāmi)
aeon (first compound member)
beginning (kalpa-ādi: 'the beginning of the aeon', loc. sg.; a + ā → ā)
to emit, send forth (visṛjāmi: present 1st sg. 'I send forth'; -i + a- → -y a-)
I (nom. sg., emphatic subject)

sentences.l: All-beings, O son-of-Kuntī, to-nature go, mine; at-the-dissolution-of-the-aeon, again them, at-the-beginning-of-the-aeon, I-send-forth.
sentences.i: All beings, Kaunteya, return to my own nature at the dissolution of an aeon, and I send them forth again at the beginning of the next.
sentences.n: This opens the chapter's cosmology of cyclical creation, completed at verse 8: at each kalpa-kṣaya, 'dissolution of the aeon', beings dissolve back into Kṛṣṇa's own prakṛti, 'nature' (translated in its ordinary sense here, rather than the philosophical guṇa-composed substrate — see note at verse 8), and he sends them forth again at each kalpa's beginning. Sandhi: पुनस्तानि is punaḥ+tāni (-aḥ+t-→-as t-); कल्पादौ is kalpa+ādau (a+ā→ā); विसृजाम्यहम् is visṛjāmi+aham (-i+a-→-y a-).

sentences.t:
प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः ।
भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात् ॥
sentences.tr:
prakṛtim svām avaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ |
bhūta-grāmam imam kṛtsnam avaśam prakṛteḥ vaśāt ||

morph.gloss: nature (acc. sg., object of avaṣṭabhya)
one's own (svām: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with prakṛtim, 'my own')
to rely on, resort to, support oneself by (avaṣṭabhya: gerund 'having relied upon'; joined before a-, no change)
to emit, send forth (present 1st sg.)
again
again (repeated, 'again and again')
being (first compound member)
multitude, collection (bhūta-grāma: 'the multitude of beings', acc. sg. masc., object of visṛjāmi)
this (imam: acc. sg. masc., agreeing with bhūtagrāmam; joined before i-, no change)
entire, whole (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with bhūtagrāmam; joined before a-, no change)
powerless, without self-control (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with bhūtagrāmam)
nature (prakṛteḥ: abl./gen. sg., 'of/by nature')
power, control, compulsion (vaśāt: abl. sg., 'by the force of'; -eḥ + v- → -er v-)

sentences.l: Nature, my-own, relying-upon, I-send-forth again and-again this whole multitude-of-beings, powerless, by-the-compulsion of-nature.
sentences.i: Relying on my own nature, I send forth again and again this whole multitude of beings, powerless, driven by the compulsion of nature.
sentences.n: This completes verse 7's picture: prakṛti here names the impersonal, mechanical substrate of manifestation (avaśam, 'powerless', describes the beings caught in it, compelled by prakṛteḥ vaśāt, 'the force of nature'), distinct from the personal Kṛṣṇa who relies upon it (svām avaṣṭabhya, 'having taken hold of [my] own [nature]') as an instrument of his will — a distinction the poem trusts the reader to hold alongside verses 4-6's language of pervasion. Sandhi: भूतग्राममिमं packs bhūta-grāmam+imam, joined; कृत्स्नमवशं is kṛtsnam+avaśam, joined; प्रकृतेर्वशात् is prakṛteḥ+vaśāt (-eḥ+v-→-er v-).

sentences.t:
न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनंजय ।
उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु ॥
sentences.tr:
na ca mām tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanaṃjaya |
udāsīna-vat āsīnam asaktam teṣu karmasu ||

morph.gloss: not
and
I (acc. sg. 'me')
those (nom. pl. neut., subject)
action (karmāṇi: nom. pl. neut., subject, in apposition to tāni)
to bind, tie down (present 3rd pl.)
'winner of wealth', an epithet of Arjuna (vocative)
indifferent, neutral, sitting apart (udāsīna-vat: adverb 'like one indifferent', formed with the adverbial/similative suffix -vat 'like, in the manner of'; -t + ā- → -d ā-, voicing before vowel)
to sit, remain (āsīna: present participle 'seated', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with the understood mām; joined before a-, no change)
unattached, not clinging (from sañj; acc. sg. masc., agreeing with the understood mām)
those/them (teṣu: loc. pl. neut. 'among them')
action (karmasu: loc. pl., 'in those actions')

sentences.l: And-not me those actions bind, O winner-of-wealth, as-one-indifferent seated, unattached, in-those actions.
sentences.i: And those actions do not bind me, Dhanañjaya, since I remain as one seated indifferently, unattached to those actions.
sentences.n: The chapter's answer to the problem posed already in chapters 3-4 (karma-bandhana, 'the bonds of action'): Kṛṣṇa is not bound by the actions of creation and dissolution just described, because he remains udāsīna-vat āsīnaḥ, 'seated as if indifferent' — the same phrase recurs at 14.23 for the guṇa-transcending sage. Dhanaṃjaya, 'winner of wealth', an epithet of Arjuna. Sandhi: उदासीनवदासीनम् packs udāsīna-vat+āsīnam (-t+ā-→-d ā-, voicing before the vowel).

sentences.t:

हेतुनानेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते ॥

the world (nom. sg. neut., subject; -t + v- → -d v-)
to revolve, turn about, evolve (viparivartate: present middle 3rd sg.)

sentences.l: With-me-as-overseer, nature brings-forth [the-world] with-its-moving-and-unmoving; by-this cause, O son-of-Kuntī, the-world revolves.
sentences.i: Under my supervision, nature gives birth to all that moves and does not move; by this cause the world turns and evolves.
sentences.n: This states the mechanism behind verses 7-9 directly: prakṛti acts, but only mayā adhyakṣeṇa, 'with me as overseer' — the personal Kṛṣṇa presiding over the impersonal process, so that jagat viparivartate, 'the world revolves', by hetunā anena, 'this cause' alone. Sandhi: मयाध्यक्षेण is mayā+adhyakṣeṇa (ā+a→ā); हेतुनानेन is hetunā+anena (ā+a→ā); जगद्विपरिवर्तते is jagat+viparivartate (-t+v-→-d v-).

sentences.t:
अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम् ।
परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम् ॥
sentences.tr:
avajānanti mām mūḍhāḥ mānuṣīm tanum āśritam |
param bhāvam ajānantaḥ mama bhūta-mahā-īśvaram ||

morph.gloss: to despise, disdain, disregard (present 3rd pl.)
I (acc. sg. 'me')
deluded, foolish (from muh; nom. pl. masc., subject; visarga dropped before the voiced m- of mānuṣīm, the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ)
human (mānuṣīm: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with tanum)
body, form (acc. sg. fem., object of āśritam)
to resort to, take refuge in, assume (āśrita: past participle used transitively, 'having assumed [a body]', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with mām; joined before ā-, no change)
higher, supreme (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with bhāvam)
nature, being, state (acc. sg. masc., object of ajānantaḥ)
to not know (ajānant: present participle 'not knowing', ajānantaḥ: nom. pl. masc., agreeing with mūḍhāḥ; -aḥ before m- → -o)
I (mama: gen. sg. 'my')
being (first compound member)
great (second member)
lord (bhūta-mahā-īśvara: 'the great lord of beings', acc. sg. masc., in apposition to param bhāvam; ā + ī → e)

sentences.l: Despise me the-deluded, human [as] a-body having-taken-on, the-higher nature not-knowing, mine, the-great-lord-of-beings.
sentences.i: The deluded despise me for taking on a human form, not knowing my higher nature as the great lord of all beings.
sentences.n: A turn to the poem's recurring complaint (cf. 4.6, 7.13, 7.24): the mūḍhāḥ, 'deluded', mistake Kṛṣṇa's mānuṣīṃ tanum, 'human body' — assumed voluntarily, āśritam, 'taken on' — for the whole of what he is, missing his param bhāvam, 'higher nature', as bhūta-mahā-īśvaraḥ, 'the great lord of beings'. Sandhi: मूढा is mūḍhāḥ with its visarga dropped (not -o) before the voiced m- of mānuṣīm, since the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ, as in verse 3's puruṣā; भावमजानन्तो packs bhāvam+ajānantaḥ (-aḥ before m-→-o); भूतमहेश्वरम् packs bhūta-mahā-īśvaram (ā+ī→e).

sentences.t:
मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः ।
राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः ॥
sentences.tr:
mogha-āśāḥ mogha-karmāṇaḥ mogha-jñānāḥ vicetasaḥ |
rākṣasīm āsurīm ca eva prakṛtim mohinīm śritāḥ ||

morph.gloss: vain, fruitless, useless (first compound member)
hope, expectation (mogha-āśa: 'whose hopes are vain', nom. pl. masc., bahuvrīhi; a + ā → ā, written joined; visarga then dropped before the voiced m- of moghakarmāṇaḥ)
vain (first compound member)
action (mogha-karman: 'whose actions are vain', nom. pl. masc.; -aḥ before m- → -o)
vain (first compound member)
knowledge (mogha-jñāna: 'whose knowledge is vain', nom. pl. masc.; visarga dropped before the voiced v- of vicetasaḥ, the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ)
confused in mind, senseless, deranged (nom. pl. masc.)
demonic, of the rākṣasas (rākṣasīm: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with prakṛtim)
demonic, of the asuras, titanic (āsurīm: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with prakṛtim; joined before ā-, no change)
and
indeed (ca + eva: a + e → ai)
nature (acc. sg., object of śritāḥ)
deluding, bewildering (mohinīm: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with prakṛtim)
to resort to, take refuge in, cling to (śrita: past participle, nom. pl. masc., predicate)

sentences.l: Of-vain-hope, of-vain-action, of-vain-knowledge, senseless — [they], a-demonic and-asuric, deluding nature, resorting-to.
sentences.i: Vain in their hopes, vain in their deeds, vain in their knowledge, senseless, they cling to a demonic, titanic, and deluding nature.
sentences.n: This describes the mūḍhāḥ of verse 11 further, in a cascade of bahuvrīhi compounds each meaning 'whose X is vain' (mogha-āśa, mogha-karman, mogha-jñāna), culminating in the diagnosis that they have taken rākṣasīm āsurīṃ ... prakṛtiṃ mohinīm, 'a demonic, titanic, and deluding nature', as their own — the same prakṛti of verses 7-10 now specified in its lower, binding aspect. Sandhi: मोघाशा packs mogha+āśāḥ (a+ā→ā, then visarga dropped before voiced m-); मोघकर्माणो is mogha-karmāṇaḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o; चैव is ca+eva (a+e→ai).

sentences.t:
महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः ।
भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम् ॥
sentences.tr:
mahā-ātmānaḥ tu mām pārtha daivīm prakṛtim āśritāḥ |
bhajanti ananya-manasaḥ jñātvā bhūta-ādim avyayam ||

morph.gloss: great (first compound member)
self, soul (mahā-ātman: 'great-souled', mahātmānaḥ: nom. pl., subject; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
but
I (acc. sg. 'me')
'son of Pṛthā', Arjuna (vocative)
divine, of the gods (daivīm: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with prakṛtim)
nature (acc. sg., object of āśritāḥ; joined before ā-, no change)
to resort to, take refuge in (āśrita: past participle, nom. pl. masc., predicate)
to worship, revere, resort to (present 3rd pl.; -i + a- → -y a-)
not other, undivided, exclusive (first compound member)
mind (ananya-manas: 'whose mind is on nothing else', nom. pl. masc.; -aḥ before j- → -o)
to know (gerund 'having known')
being (first compound member)
origin, beginning (bhūta-ādi: 'the origin of beings', acc. sg. masc., in apposition to an understood mām; a + ā → ā)
imperishable, undiminishing (acc. sg. masc., in apposition; joined before a-, no change)

sentences.l: But-the-great-souled, me, O son-of-Pṛthā, the-divine nature having-resorted-to, worship-with-minds-on-nothing-else, having-known [me as] the-origin-of-beings, imperishable.
sentences.i: But the great souls, Pārtha, who take refuge in my divine nature, worship me with undivided minds, knowing me as the origin of beings, the imperishable.
sentences.n: The contrasting portrait to verses 11-12: where the mūḍhāḥ resort to a demonic nature, the mahātmānaḥ, 'great souls', resort instead to Kṛṣṇa's daivīṃ prakṛtim, 'divine nature', worshiping ananya-manasaḥ, 'with minds on nothing else' — the same undivided devotion recurs at verses 22 and 30. Sandhi: महात्मानस्तु is mahātmānaḥ+tu (-aḥ+t-→-as t-); भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो packs bhajanti (-i+a-→-y a-) + ananya-manasa�ḥ (-aḥ before j-→-o).

sentences.t:
सततं कीर्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः ।
नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ॥
sentences.tr:
satatam kīrtayantaḥ mām yatantaḥ ca dṛḍha-vratāḥ |
namasyantaḥ ca mām bhaktyā nitya-yuktāḥ upāsate ||

morph.gloss: always, constantly (adverb)
to praise, glorify, proclaim (kīrtayant: present participle 'praising', kīrtayantaḥ: nom. pl. masc.; -aḥ before m- → -o)
I (acc. sg. 'me')
to strive, exert oneself (yatant: present participle 'striving', yatantaḥ: nom. pl. masc.; -aḥ + c- → -aś c-)
and
firm, fixed (first compound member)
vow (dṛḍha-vrata: 'of firm vows', nom. pl. masc.)
to bow to, do homage to (denominative from namas; present participle, namasyantaḥ: nom. pl. masc.; -aḥ + c- → -aś c-)
and
I (acc. sg. 'me')
devotion (instr. sg., 'with devotion')
constant (first compound member)
to join, discipline (yukta: past participle, nitya-yukta: 'ever disciplined', nom. pl. masc.; visarga dropped before the vowel u- of upāsate, the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ)
to worship, revere, sit close to (present middle 3rd pl.)

sentences.l: Constantly praising me and-striving, of-firm-vows, and-doing-homage-to me with-devotion, ever-disciplined, they-worship.
sentences.i: Constantly glorifying me, striving with firm resolve, bowing to me in devotion, ever disciplined, they worship me.
sentences.n: This elaborates verse 13's worship in practical terms — praising (kīrtayantaḥ), striving (yatantaḥ), bowing (namasyantaḥ) — all done nitya-yuktāḥ, 'ever disciplined', the same constancy already named in 8.14's nitya-yuktasya yoginaḥ. Sandhi: कीर्तयन्तो is kīrtayantaḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o (a pattern now well established, occurring more than a dozen times in this chapter and not separately flagged from here on except where a new consonant is involved); यतन्तश्च and नमस्यन्तश्च both show -aḥ+c-→-aś c-.

sentences.t:
ज्ञानयज्ञेन चाप्यन्ये यजन्तो मामुपासते ।
एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन बहुधा विश्वतोमुखम् ॥
sentences.tr:
jñāna-yajñena ca api anye yajantaḥ mām upāsate |
ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvataḥ-mukham ||

morph.gloss: knowledge (first compound member)
sacrifice (jñāna-yajña: 'the sacrifice of knowledge', instr. sg., 'by the sacrifice of knowledge')
and
also (ca + api: a + a → ā)
other (anye: nom. pl. masc., 'others'; api + anye: i + a → y a-)
to sacrifice, worship (yajant: present participle, yajantaḥ: nom. pl. masc.; -aḥ before m- → -o)
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me'; joined before u-, no change)
to worship (present middle 3rd pl.)
one (ekatva: 'oneness, unity', instr. sg., 'as one, in identity')
separate, distinct (pṛthaktva: 'separateness, distinction', instr. sg., 'as separate, in duality')
variously, in many ways (adverb)
on all sides, in every direction (first compound member)
face (viśvatas-mukha: 'facing every direction, universal-faced', acc. sg., agreeing with mām; -aḥ + m- → -o)

sentences.l: By-the-sacrifice-of-knowledge and-also-others, sacrificing, me worship, as-one, as-separate, in-many-ways, facing-every-direction.
sentences.i: And others, worshiping through the sacrifice of knowledge, revere me as one, as separate [from themselves], or in the manifold form that faces every direction.
sentences.n: A third mode of approaching Kṛṣṇa, alongside the devotional worship of verses 13-14: jñāna-yajña, 'the sacrifice of knowledge', by which some worship him ekatvena, 'as one' (i.e. as identical with the self, the non-dual reading), others pṛthaktvena, 'as separate' (a distinct personal God), and others still bahudhā viśvato-mukham, 'in many forms, facing every direction' (worship of the universal or manifold divine form, anticipating the theophany of chapter 11). Sandhi: चाप्यन्ये packs ca+api (a+a→ā) + api+anye (i+a→y a-); यजन्तो is yajantaḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o.

sentences.t:
अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाहमहमौषधम् ।
मन्त्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम् ॥
sentences.tr:
aham kratuḥ aham yajñaḥ svadhā aham aham auṣadham |
mantraḥ aham aham eva ājyam aham agniḥ aham hutam ||

morph.gloss: I (nom. sg., subject)
a Vedic sacrificial rite, specifically a Soma-rite (nom. sg., predicate; -uḥ + a- → -ur a-)
I (nom. sg., subject)
sacrifice (nom. sg., predicate)
the oblation offered to the ancestors, the sacred formula accompanying it (nom. sg., predicate; svadhā + aham: ā + a → ā, written joined)
I (repeated; aham + aham: no vowel sandhi — aham ends in the consonant -m, so this is simply written joined before the following vowel, with no phonetic change)
medicinal herb, healing plant (nom. sg. neut., predicate; aham + auṣadham: likewise no vowel sandhi, simply written joined before au-)

words.reading: mantraḥ aham aham eva ājyam aham agniḥ aham

glyphs.tr: mantraḥ aham aham eva ājyam aham agniḥ aham

morph.gloss: sacred formula, hymn (nom. sg., predicate; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
I (nom. sg., subject)
I (nom. sg., subject)
indeed, also
clarified butter, ghee, used in oblations (nom. sg. neut., predicate; eva + ājyam: a + ā → ā)
I (nom. sg., subject; joined before a-, no change)
fire (nom. sg., predicate)
I (nom. sg., subject)
to offer as oblation, pour into the fire (huta: past participle 'that which is offered, the oblation', nom. sg. neut., predicate)

sentences.l: I [am] the-kratu, I [am] the-sacrifice, the-svadhā I, I [am] the-medicinal-herb; the-mantra I, I indeed [am] the-ghee, I [am] the-fire, I [am] the-oblation.
sentences.i: I am the sacrificial rite, I am the sacrifice, I am the offering to the ancestors, I am the healing herb; I am the sacred formula, I am also the clarified butter, I am the fire, and I am what is poured into it.
sentences.n: The first of the chapter's two great catalog verses (with verse 17): Kṛṣṇa identifies himself with every element of the Vedic sacrifice — the rite itself (kratu), the sacrifice (yajña), the ancestral offering (svadhā), the healing herb used in it (auṣadha), the sacred formula spoken over it (mantra), the ghee poured (ājya), the fire it feeds (agni), and the oblation itself (huta) — collapsing the entire ritual apparatus into a single identity, so that no part of sacrifice stands outside him. Sandhi: क्रतुरहं is kratuḥ+aham (-uḥ+a-→-ur a-); स्वधाहमहमौषधम् packs svadhā+aham (ā+a→ā, genuine vowel sandhi, since svadhā ends in ā), then aham+aham and aham+auṣadham, both simply written joined before a following vowel with no phonetic change, since aham ends in the consonant -m, not a vowel; मन्त्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं packs mantraḥ+aham (avagraha) + eva+ājyam (a+ā→ā), with the remaining aham's simply written joined before vowels without further change.

sentences.t:
पिताहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः ।
वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक्साम यजुरेव च ॥
sentences.tr:
pitā aham asya jagataḥ mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ |
vedyam pavitram oṃkāraḥ ṛk sāma yajuḥ eva ca ||

morph.gloss: father (pitā: nom. sg., predicate; pitā + aham: ā + a → ā, written joined)
I (nom. sg., subject; joined before a-, no change)
this (asya: gen. sg. neut., 'of this world')
the world (jagataḥ: gen. sg.; -aḥ before m- → -o)
mother (mātā: nom. sg., predicate)
ordainer, disposer, creator (dhātā: nom. sg., predicate, agent noun from √dhā)
grandfather (from pitṛ + mahā; nom. sg., predicate)
to know (vedya: gerundive 'to be known, the object of knowledge', nom. sg. neut., predicate)
purifier, that which purifies (nom. sg. neut., predicate; joined before o-, no change)
the syllable Om (nom. sg., predicate; visarga drops before the vowel ṛ- of the next word, no other change, as before any non-a vowel)
a verse of the Ṛgveda, the Ṛgveda itself (nom. sg., predicate; -c + s- → -k s-, consonant assimilation)
a chant of the Sāmaveda, the Sāmaveda itself (nom. sg. neut., predicate)
a Yajurveda formula, the Yajurveda itself (yajuḥ: nom. sg. neut., predicate; -uḥ + e- → -ur e-)
indeed, too
and

sentences.l: The-father I of-this world, the-mother, the-ordainer, the-grandfather; the-object-of-knowledge, the-purifier, the-syllable-Om, the-Ṛc and-the-Sāman, and the-Yajus indeed.
sentences.i: I am the father of this world, its mother, its ordainer, its grandfather; I am what is to be known, the purifier, the syllable Om, and the Ṛgveda, the Sāmaveda and the Yajurveda as well.
sentences.n: The second catalog verse continues verse 16's identification, now with the roles of kinship (father, mother, ordainer, grandfather) and then with the sacred syllable Om and the three Vedas themselves (ṛc, sāman, yajus) — echoing 7.8's 'the syllable Om in all the Vedas' but now naming each Veda by name. Ṛk-sāma is one printed token joining two separate words, ṛc (reverting to its guttural allomorph -k before s-) and sāman. Sandhi: पिताहमस्य packs pitā+aham (ā+a→ā) + aham+asya, joined; जगतो is jagataḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o; पवित्रमोंकार shows oṃkāraḥ's own visarga simply dropping before the following word's initial ṛ- (a non-a vowel), the same rule already seen for -āḥ before voiced consonants but here applying to any vowel; यजुरेव is yajuḥ+eva (-uḥ+e-→-ur e-, matching kratuḥ+aham's pattern in verse 16 but now before a vowel rather than a nasal-initial word).

sentences.t:
गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् ।
प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥
sentences.tr:

prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānam nidhānam bījam avyayam ||

friend, well-wisher, 'good-hearted' (nom. sg., predicate)
origin, source, arising (nom. sg., predicate)

place, station, foundation (nom. sg. neut., predicate)
receptacle, repository, treasure-house (nom. sg. neut., predicate)
seed (nom. sg. neut., predicate; joined before a-, no change)
imperishable, undiminishing (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with bījam)

sentences.l: The-goal, the-supporter, the-lord, the-witness, the-abode, the-refuge, the-friend, the-origin, the-dissolution, the-station, the-treasure-house, the-imperishable seed.
sentences.i: I am the goal, the sustainer, the lord, the witness, the dwelling, the refuge, the friend; I am the source, the end, the foundation, the treasury, and the imperishable seed.
sentences.n: A third catalog, without the repeated 'I am' of verses 16-17 but continuing the same construction (each noun a further predicate nominative in apposition to an implied aham): twelve names for Kṛṣṇa as the world's beginning, end and constant support, closing on bījam avyayam, 'the imperishable seed' — the same organic image of a seed containing its own unfolding used elsewhere for prakṛti and puruṣa together. Sandhi: गतिर्भर्ता is gatiḥ+bhartā (-iḥ+bh-→-ir bh-); बीजमव्ययम् is bījam+avyayam, joined.

sentences.t:
तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च ।
अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन ॥
sentences.tr:
tapāmi aham aham varṣam nigṛhṇāmi utsṛjāmi ca |
amṛtam ca eva mṛtyuḥ ca sat asat ca aham arjuna ||

morph.gloss: to heat, radiate warmth (tapāmi: present 1st sg. 'I give heat', as the sun; -i + a- → -y a-)
I (nom. sg., subject)
I (nom. sg., subject; repeated; tapāmi + aham + aham fused into one printed token)
rain (acc. sg. neut., object of nigṛhṇāmi and utsṛjāmi)
to withhold, restrain, hold back (nigṛhṇāmi: present 1st sg. 'I withhold')
to send forth, release (utsṛjāmi: present 1st sg. 'I release'; -i + u- → -y u-)
and
immortality, the deathless, the nectar of immortality (nom. sg. neut., predicate)
and
indeed (ca + eva: a + e → ai)
death (mṛtyuḥ: nom. sg., predicate; -uḥ + c- → -uś c-)

sentences.l: I-give-heat; I withhold-and-release the-rain; immortality and-indeed death, and-being and-non-being I, O Arjuna.
sentences.i: I give forth heat; I hold back the rain and I send it out again. I am immortality and also death, and I am being and non-being too, Arjuna.
sentences.n: The catalog verses close by pairing opposites within Kṛṣṇa himself: heat and rain (a nod to his control of the sun and monsoon), amṛta and mṛtyu ('the deathless' and 'death'), and finally sat and asat, 'being' and 'non-being' — the same pair used at 13.12 and 11.37 for the ultimate reality beyond ordinary categories. The first token of the verse fuses three words: tapāmi+aham+aham. Sandhi: निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि is nigṛhṇāmi+utsṛjāmi (-i+u-→-y u-); मृत्युश्च is mṛtyuḥ+ca (-uḥ+c-→-uś c-); सदसच्चाहमर्जुन packs sat+asat (-t+a-→-d a-) + asat+ca (-t+c-→-c c-) + ca+aham (a+a→ā), all fused into one printed word.

sentences.t:
त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापा ।
यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते ।
ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोक- ।
मश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान् ॥
sentences.tr:
traividyāḥ mām soma-pāḥ pūta-pāpāḥ |
yajñaiḥ iṣṭvā svar-gatim prārthayante |
te puṇyam āsādya sura-indra-loka- |
m aśnanti divyān divi deva-bhogān ||

morph.gloss: versed in the three Vedas (traividya: nom. pl. masc., subject; visarga dropped before the voiced m- of mām, the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ)
I (acc. sg. 'me')
Soma, the sacred sacrificial drink (first compound member)
to drink (agent noun, soma-pā: 'Soma-drinker', nom. pl. masc., subject; visarga retained as -ḥ before the voiceless p- of pūtapāpāḥ)
to purify (pūta: past participle 'purified', first compound member)
sin, evil (pūta-pāpa: 'whose sins are purified, cleansed of sin', nom. pl. masc., subject; visarga dropped before the voiced y- of yajñaiḥ across the line-break, the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ)
sacrifice (yajñaiḥ: instr. pl., 'by sacrifices'; -aiḥ + i- → -air i-)
to sacrifice, worship (iṣṭvā: gerund 'having sacrificed, having worshiped')
heaven (first compound member)
going, course, goal (svar-gati: 'the goal of heaven, heaven-going', acc. sg. fem., object of prārthayante)
to pray for, long for, aspire to (denominative; present middle 3rd pl.)
they (nom. pl. masc., subject)
merit, meritorious (puṇyam: acc. sg. neut., object of āsādya; joined before ā-, no change)
to reach, arrive at, attain (āsādya: gerund 'having reached')
a god, deity (first compound member)
Indra, chief of the gods (sura-indra: 'Indra of the gods', second member; a + i → e)
world (sura-indra-loka: 'the world of Indra', acc. sg. neut., object of aśnanti; the Wikisource print line breaks this compound oddly across the line — see note)
world (m: the final consonant of lokam, completing the word begun on the previous print line — see note)
to eat, partake of (aśnanti: present 3rd pl. 'they enjoy')
divine, heavenly (divyān: acc. pl. masc., agreeing with devabhogān; written joined before d-, no change)
heaven, the sky (divi: loc. sg. 'in heaven')
god, deity (first compound member)
enjoyment, pleasure (deva-bhoga: 'the pleasures of the gods', acc. pl. masc., object of aśnanti)

sentences.l: The-threefold-Veda-knowers, Soma-drinkers, purified-of-sin, me having-sacrificed with-sacrifices, pray-for the-goal-of-heaven; they, having-attained that merit, enjoy Indra's-world-of-the-gods — divine, in-heaven, the-pleasures-of-the-gods.
sentences.i: Those versed in the three Vedas, who drink the soma and are purified of sin, worship me with sacrifices and pray to reach heaven; having earned that merit, they reach the heaven of Indra and there enjoy the divine pleasures of the gods.
sentences.n: The chapter's first four-line (triṣṭubh) verse turns to a pointed critique of Vedic ritualists (traividyāḥ, 'knowers of the three Vedas', somapāḥ, 'Soma-drinkers'): their worship does reach Kṛṣṇa (yajñair iṣṭvā, 'having sacrificed with sacrifices' — the object is explicitly named, mām, 'me', not merely understood; cf. verse 24) and does win them heaven, but only a temporary one, as verse 21 goes on to say. The Wikisource print line breaks the compound sura-indra-lokam, 'the world of Indra of the gods', oddly across the line, splitting it into सुरेन्द्रलोक- and मश्नन्ति; the two are one continuous phrase (sura-indra-lokam + aśnanti, 'they enjoy the world of Indra') and are drafted here as two words-entries only to tile the source exactly, on the model of ch02 verse 6's jijīviṣāmaḥ/te 'vasthitāḥ split. Sandhi: सोमपाः retains its visarga unchanged (-ḥ) before the voiceless p- of pūtapāpāḥ; पूतपापा drops its visarga before the voiced य- of yajñaiḥ across the line-break, since the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ; यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा is yajñaiḥ+iṣṭvā (-aiḥ+i-→-air i-); दिव्यान्दिवि packs divyān+divi, written joined with no change (-n before d-).

sentences.t:
ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालं ।
क्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति ।
एवं त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्ना ।
गतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते ॥
sentences.tr:
te tam bhuktvā svarga-lokam viśālam |
kṣīṇe puṇye martya-lokam viśanti |
evam trayī-dharmam anuprapannāḥ |
gata-āgatam kāma-kāmāḥ labhante ||

morph.gloss: they (nom. pl. masc., subject)
that (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with svargalokam)
to enjoy, partake of (bhuktvā: gerund 'having enjoyed')
heaven (first compound member)
world (svarga-loka: 'the heaven-world', acc. sg. masc., object of bhuktvā)
vast, extensive (acc. sg. masc., agreeing with svargalokam)
to wane, diminish, be exhausted (kṣīṇa: past participle, loc. sg. neut., locative absolute with puṇye)
merit (loc. sg. neut., 'when merit is exhausted')
mortal (first compound member)
world (martya-loka: 'the world of mortals', acc. sg. masc., object of viśanti)
to enter (present 3rd pl.)
thus, in this way (adverb)
the triad, the three Vedas collectively (first compound member)

law, observance (trayī-dharma: 'the law of the triple Veda', i.e. Vedic ritual religion — treated like kula-dharma as a specific named body of observance rather than the cosmic/social sense, and so translated rather than left as bare 'dharma'; acc. sg. masc., object of anuprapannāḥ; joined before a-, no change)

to follow after, resort to, take up (anuprapanna: past participle 'having resorted to, having followed', nom. pl. masc., agreeing with te; visarga dropped before the voiced g- of gatāgatam across the line-break, the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ)
to go (gata: past participle, first compound member, 'gone')
to come (āgata: past participle, second member, 'come'; gata-āgata: 'the going and the coming', i.e. repeated transmigration, acc. sg. neut., object of labhante; a + ā → ā)
desire, sensual pleasure (first compound member)

desire (repeated as second member; kāma-kāma: 'desirer of desires, one whose desire is for sense-pleasures', nom. pl. masc., subject; visarga dropped before the voiced l- of labhante, the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ)
to obtain, attain (present middle 3rd pl.)

sentences.l: They, that heaven-world, vast, having-enjoyed, when-merit [is] exhausted, the-mortal-world enter; thus the-law-of-the-triple-Veda having-followed, the-going-and-coming, desirers-of-desires, obtain.
sentences.i: Having enjoyed that vast world of heaven, they enter the world of mortals again once their merit is used up; thus, having followed the discipline of the triple Veda, desiring only desires, they win nothing but a coming and going.
sentences.n: This completes verse 20's critique: the heaven so won is finite — kṣīṇe puṇye, 'when the merit [that bought it] is exhausted' — and its enjoyers fall back to martya-lokam, 'the world of mortals'. Gata-āgatam, 'the going and the coming', names the resulting cycle directly, and kāma-kāmāḥ, 'desirers of desires' (a doubled-root bahuvrīhi echoing verse 9's udāsīna-vat construction), diagnoses its cause: desire for particular results rather than for Kṛṣṇa himself, the same critique leveled at Vedic ritualists since 2.42-44. Trayī-dharma, 'the law of the triple Veda', i.e. Vedic ritual religion, is translated here rather than left as bare 'dharma': like kula-dharma (ch. 1's 'family-laws'), it names one specific, nameable body of observance — the ritual religion of the three Vedas — rather than the cosmic or social order that convention leaves untranslated, so L renders it 'the-law-of-the-triple-Veda' and I 'the discipline of the triple Veda'. Sandhi: त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्ना packs trayī-dharmam+anuprapannāḥ, joined, with the compound's own visarga then dropping before the voiced ग- of gatāgatam across the line-break; गतागतं is gata+āgatam (a+ā→ā); कामकामा is kāma-kāmāḥ, visarga dropped before the voiced ल- of labhante.

sentences.t:
अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते ।
तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥
sentences.tr:
ananyāḥ cintayantaḥ mām ye janāḥ paryupāsate |
teṣām nitya-abhiyuktānām yoga-kṣemam vahāmi aham ||

morph.gloss: not other, exclusively (nom. pl. masc.; -āḥ + c- → -āś c-)
to think of, meditate on (cintayant: present participle 'thinking of', cintayantaḥ: nom. pl. masc.; -aḥ before m- → -o)
I (acc. sg. 'me')
who (ye: nom. pl. masc. relative)
person, people (nom. pl., subject)
to worship attentively, serve devotedly (present middle 3rd pl.)
them (teṣām: gen. pl., 'of them')
constant (first compound member)
to be devoted to, engaged with (abhiyukta: past participle, nitya-abhiyukta: 'ever devoted', gen. pl., agreeing with teṣām; a + a → ā)
here not the discipline but 'acquisition, obtaining [of what is not yet possessed]' (first compound member; see note)
preservation, safekeeping [of what is already possessed] (yoga-kṣema: 'acquisition and preservation, welfare', acc. sg. neut., object of vahāmi)
to carry, bear (vahāmi: present 1st sg. 'I carry'; -i + a- → -y a-)
I (nom. sg., subject)

sentences.l: Not-other, thinking-of me, who people worship-attentively — of-them, ever-devoted, the-getting-and-keeping I-carry.
sentences.i: For those who, with undivided minds, keep me in their thoughts and worship me with constant devotion, I personally look after what they need and what they already have.
sentences.n: This turns from the fate of ritualists (verses 20-21) to the security promised to Kṛṣṇa's own devotees: ananyāḥ ... cintayantaḥ, 'undistracted, thinking [only of me]' (the same ananya- pattern as verses 13, 14, 30), and yoga-kṣemam vahāmi, 'I carry the yoga-kṣema'. Here yoga does not carry its usual sense of spiritual discipline (kept untranslated elsewhere in this chapter, e.g. verses 5 and 28) but belongs to the fixed idiom yoga-kṣema, 'acquisition and preservation' — getting what one lacks and keeping what one has — a common Sanskrit compound for material welfare or security; it is translated here for clarity rather than left untranslated, since rendering it literally as 'yoga' would suggest the wrong sense entirely. Sandhi: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो packs ananyāḥ+cintayantaḥ (-āḥ+c-→-āś c-) + cintayantaḥ+mām (-aḥ before m-→-o); नित्याभियुक्तानां is nitya+abhiyuktānām (a+a→ā).

sentences.t:
येऽप्यन्यदेवताभक्ता यजन्ते श्रद्धयान्विताः ।
तेऽपि मामेव कौन्तेय यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम् ॥
sentences.tr:
ye api anya-devatā-bhaktāḥ yajante śraddhayā anvitāḥ |
te api mām eva kaunteya yajanti avidhi-pūrvakam ||

morph.gloss: who (ye: nom. pl. masc. relative; ye + api: e + a → e with avagraha)
even, also (api + anya: i + a → y a-)
other (first compound member)
deity, god (second member)
devoted, past participle of bhaj (anya-devatā-bhakta: 'devoted to other deities', nom. pl. masc., subject; visarga dropped before the voiced y- of yajante, the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ)
to sacrifice, worship (present middle 3rd pl.)
faith (śraddhayā: instr. sg., 'with faith')
to accompany, be endowed with (anvita: past participle 'endowed with, accompanied by', nom. pl. masc., agreeing with the subject; śraddhayā + anvitāḥ: ā + a → ā, written joined)
they (te: nom. pl. masc., subject; te + api: e + a → e with avagraha)
too, even
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me')
alone, indeed
'son of Kuntī', Arjuna (vocative)
to sacrifice, worship (yajanti: present 3rd pl.; -i + a- → -y a-)
without proper rule, contrary to the prescribed rite (first compound member)
preceded by, done in accordance with (a-vidhi-pūrvaka: 'not in accordance with the correct rule or method', acc. sg. neut., adverbial)

sentences.l: Who even, to-other-deities-devoted, sacrifice with-faith-endowed — they too me alone, O son-of-Kuntī, worship without-the-proper-rite.
sentences.i: Even those who worship other gods, if they do so with faith, are really worshiping me, though not in the correct way.
sentences.n: A generous verse often quoted on its own: even anya-devatā-bhaktāḥ, 'those devoted to other deities', when they worship śraddhayā anvitāḥ, 'endowed with faith', are in fact worshiping Kṛṣṇa himself (mām eva), though avidhi-pūrvakam, 'not according to the proper method' — since they do not recognize the true object of their devotion, a point verse 24 explains. Sandhi: येऽप्यन्यदेवताभक्ता packs ye+api (avagraha) + api+anya (i+a→y a-), with the compound's own visarga dropping before the voiced य- of yajante; तेऽपि is te+api (avagraha); यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम् is yajanti+avidhi-pūrvakam (-i+a-→-y a-).

sentences.t:
अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च ।
न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति ते ॥
sentences.tr:
aham hi sarva-yajñānām bhoktā ca prabhuḥ eva ca |
na tu mām abhijānanti tattvena atas cyavanti te ||

morph.gloss: I (nom. sg., subject)
for, indeed
all (first compound member)
sacrifice (sarva-yajña: 'all sacrifices', gen. pl., 'of all sacrifices')
to enjoy, partake of (bhoktṛ: agent noun 'enjoyer, partaker', bhoktā: nom. sg., predicate)
and
lord, master (prabhuḥ: nom. sg., predicate; -uḥ + e- → -ur e-)
indeed
and
not
but
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me'; joined before a-, no change)
to know truly, recognize (present 3rd pl.)
true nature, reality, essence (tattvena: instr. sg., 'in [my] true reality, truly'; tattvena + ataḥ: a + a → ā)
therefore, hence (ataḥ: -aḥ + c- → -aś c-)
to fall away, lapse, decline (cyavanti: present 3rd pl.)
they (nom. pl. masc., subject)

sentences.l: I indeed of-all-sacrifices [am] the-enjoyer and the-lord too; but not me they-truly-know, therefore-in-reality they-lapse.
sentences.i: For I am the one who enjoys and presides over every sacrifice; but people do not know me as I truly am, and so they fall away.
sentences.n: This explains verse 23's avidhi-pūrvakam: Kṛṣṇa is bhoktā ca prabhuḥ eva ca, 'both the enjoyer and the lord', of every sacrifice whatsoever, but those who worship other deities do not know this tattvena, 'in [my true] reality', and so cyavanti, 'fall away' — presumably back into the cycle of rebirth described for ritualists in verses 20-21. Sandhi: प्रभुरेव is prabhuḥ+eva (-uḥ+e-→-ur e-); मामभिजानन्ति is mām+abhijānanti, joined; तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति packs tattvena+ataḥ (ā+a→ā) + ataḥ+cyavanti (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-).

sentences.t:
यान्ति देवव्रता देवान्पितॄन्यान्ति पितृव्रताः ।
भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम् ॥
sentences.tr:
yānti deva-vratāḥ devān pitṝn yānti pitṛ-vratāḥ |
bhūtāni yānti bhūta-ijyāḥ yānti mad-yājinaḥ api mām ||

morph.gloss: to go (present 3rd pl.)
god, deity (first compound member)
vow (deva-vrata: 'vowed to the gods, devoted to the gods', nom. pl. masc., subject; visarga dropped before the voiced d- of devān, the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ)
god, deity (devān: acc. pl. masc., object of the preceding yānti)
father, ancestor (pitṝn: acc. pl. masc., object of the following yānti; devān + pitṝn: -n before p-, no change, written joined)
to go (yānti: present 3rd pl.; pitṝn + yānti: -n before y-, no change, written joined)
father, ancestor (first compound member)
vow (pitṛ-vrata: 'vowed to the ancestors, devoted to the ancestors', nom. pl. masc., subject)
being (acc. pl. neut., object of yānti)
to go (present 3rd pl.)
being (first compound member)

sacrifice, worship (bhūta-ijyā: 'one who sacrifices to spirits/beings', nom. pl. masc., subject; a + i → e; visarga dropped before the voiced y- of the following yānti, the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ)
to go (present 3rd pl.)
me (stem form, first compound member)
one who sacrifices, a worshiper (mad-yājin: 'my worshiper', nom. pl. masc., subject; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
even, too
I (acc. sg. 'me')

sentences.l: Go the-gods-vowed to-the-gods; to-the-ancestors go the-ancestors-vowed; to-the-beings go the-beings'-sacrificers; go my-worshipers too to-me.
sentences.i: Those devoted to the gods go to the gods, those devoted to the ancestors go to the ancestors, those who sacrifice to spirits go to the spirits — but my worshipers come to me.
sentences.n: A chiastic list matching each kind of worshiper to the destination proper to their worship: deva-vratāḥ, 'those vowed to the gods', reach the gods; pitṛ-vratāḥ, the ancestors (pitṝn); bhūta-ijyāḥ, 'sacrificers to spirits', the bhūtāni themselves; but mad-yājinaḥ, 'my worshipers', reach mām, Kṛṣṇa — a point already made in general terms at 7.23, restated here as yānti deva-vratā devān and now specified for the devotee's own case. Sandhi: देवव्रता is deva-vratāḥ, visarga dropped before voiced द-; देवान्पितॄन्यान्ति fuses three words, devān+pitṝn+yānti, written joined with no phonetic change since -n before a stop or semivowel is unaffected; भूतेज्या is bhūta+ijyāḥ (a+i→e); मद्याजिनोऽपि is mad-yājinaḥ+api (avagraha).

sentences.t:
पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति ।
तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
sentences.tr:
patram puṣpam phalam toyam yaḥ me bhaktyā prayacchati |
tat aham bhakti-upahṛtam aśnāmi prayata-ātmanaḥ ||

morph.gloss: leaf (acc. sg. neut., object of prayacchati)
flower (acc. sg. neut., object of prayacchati)
fruit (acc. sg. neut., object of prayacchati)
water (acc. sg. neut., object of prayacchati)
who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative; -aḥ before m- → -o)
I (me: gen./dat. sg. enclitic 'to me')
devotion (instr. sg., 'with devotion')
to offer, present, give (present 3rd sg.)
that (tat: acc. sg. neut., object of aśnāmi; -t + a- → -d a-)
I (nom. sg., subject)
devotion (first compound member)
to bring near, present, offer (upahṛta: past participle 'offered, presented', bhakti-upahṛta: 'offered with devotion', acc. sg. neut., in apposition to tat; i + u → yu)
to eat, partake of (aśnāmi: present 1st sg.; joined before a-, no change)
to restrain, control (prayata: past participle 'controlled, disciplined, of pure mind', first compound member)
self, soul (prayata-ātman: 'of disciplined, pure self', gen. sg., referring to the devotee; a + ā → ā)

sentences.l: A-leaf, a-flower, a-fruit, water — who to-me with-devotion offers, that, offered-with-devotion, I-accept, of-one-whose-self-is-disciplined.
sentences.i: Whoever offers me a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water with devotion, I accept that offering, made with devotion, from one of disciplined mind.
sentences.n: The famous verse on the simplicity of devotional offering: patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyam, 'a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water' — the humblest possible gifts — are enough, so long as they come bhaktyā, 'with devotion', from one who is prayata-ātmā, 'of disciplined, pure self'. Note that pra-yam gives both the verb 'offers' (prayacchati) in the first half and the participle 'disciplined, restrained' (prayata) in the second — the same root used for both giving and self-control. Sandhi: तदहं is tat+aham (-t+a-→-d a-); भक्त्युपहृतम् is bhakti+upahṛtam (i+u→yu); प्रयतात्मनः is prayata+ātmanaḥ (a+ā→ā).

sentences.t:
यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् ।
यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् ॥
sentences.tr:
yat karoṣi yat aśnāsi yat juhoṣi dadāsi yat |
yat tapasyasi kaunteya tat kuruṣva mad-arpaṇam ||

morph.gloss: whatever (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, repeated throughout the verse; -t + k- → -t k-, no change, k voiceless)
whatever (yat: repeated; -t + a- → -d a-)
to eat, partake of (aśnāsi: present 2nd sg.)
whatever (yat: repeated; -t + j- → -j j-)
to offer in sacrifice, pour as oblation (juhoṣi: present 2nd sg.)
to give (present 2nd sg.)
whatever (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, repeated)
whatever (yat: repeated; -t + t- → -t t-, assimilation)
to practice austerity (tapasya: denominative 'to practice austerity', tapasyasi: present 2nd sg.)
'son of Kuntī', Arjuna (vocative)
that (tat: acc. sg. neut., object of kuruṣva)
to do, make (kuruṣva: imperative middle 2nd sg. 'do!, make [it]!'; joined before k-, no change)
me (stem form, first compound member)
offering, dedication, presentation (mad-arpaṇa: 'an offering to me', acc. sg. neut., in apposition to tat)

sentences.l: Whatever you-do, whatever you-eat, whatever you-offer-in-sacrifice, [whatever] you-give, whatever austerity-you-practice, O son-of-Kuntī — that do as-an-offering-to-me.
sentences.i: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice or give away, whatever austerity you perform, Kaunteya — do it as an offering to me.
sentences.n: A fivefold yat ... yat ... construction (whatever you do / eat / sacrifice / give / practice as austerity) generalizes verse 26's teaching from ritual offerings to every act of life, closing with the instruction tat kuruṣva mad-arpaṇam, 'do that as an offering to me' — the practical heart of the chapter's devotional teaching, echoing 3.9's insistence that action done as sacrifice does not bind. Sandhi: यत् shows its final -t assimilating differently before each following consonant — unchanged before the voiceless k- of karoṣi, voiced to -d before the vowel a- of aśnāsi, assimilated to -j before the j- of juhoṣi, and doubled to -t before the t- of tapasyasi; तत्कुरुष्व is tat+kuruṣva, joined, no change before k-.

sentences.t:
शुभाशुभफलैरेवं मोक्ष्यसे कर्मबन्धनैः ।
संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा विमुक्तो मामुपैष्यसि ॥
sentences.tr:
śubha-aśubha-phalaiḥ evam mokṣyase karma-bandhanaiḥ |
saṃnyāsa-yoga-yukta-ātmā vimuktaḥ mām upaiṣyasi ||

morph.gloss: good, auspicious (first compound member)
bad, inauspicious (second member; śubha + aśubha: a + a → ā)
fruit, result (śubha-aśubha-phala: 'good and bad fruits', instr. pl.)
thus (phalaiḥ + evam: -aiḥ + e- → -air e-, written joined)
to release, free (mokṣyase: future middle 2nd sg. 'you shall be released')
action (first compound member)
bond, fetter (karma-bandhana: 'the bonds of action', instr. pl., 'from the bonds of action')
renunciation (first compound member)
yoga, kept untranslated (second member)
to join, discipline (yukta: past participle, saṃnyāsa-yoga-yukta: 'disciplined by the yoga of renunciation', third member)
self, soul (yukta-ātman: nom. sg. masc., subject, 'whose self is disciplined'; a + ā → ā)
to release, free (vimukta: past participle 'freed, liberated', nom. sg. masc.; -aḥ before m- → -o)
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me'; joined before u-, no change)
to come to, attain, reach (upaiṣyasi: future 2nd sg.)

sentences.l: By-good-and-bad-fruits thus you-shall-be-released from-the-bonds-of-action; with-self-disciplined-by-the-yoga-of-renunciation, freed, to-me-you-shall-come.
sentences.i: In this way you will be freed from the bonds of action, whether their fruits are good or bad; with your self disciplined by the yoga of renunciation, once liberated, you will come to me.
sentences.n: This draws the practical conclusion from verse 27: acting as an offering to Kṛṣṇa releases one even from śubha-aśubha-phalaiḥ karma-bandhanaiḥ, 'the bonds of action [that bear] good and bad fruits alike' — echoing 2.50's buddhi-yukto jahāti iha ubhe sukṛta-duṣkṛte. Saṃnyāsa-yoga-yukta-ātmā, 'whose self is disciplined by the yoga of renunciation', names the resulting state, leading to mokṣa (vimuktaḥ) and finally to Kṛṣṇa himself (mām upaiṣyasi). Sandhi: शुभाशुभफलैरेवं packs śubha+aśubha (a+a→ā) + phalaiḥ+evam (-aiḥ+e-→-air e-); संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा ends in yukta+ātmā (a+ā→ā); विमुक्तो is vimuktaḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o.

sentences.t:
समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः ।
ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् ॥
sentences.tr:
samaḥ aham sarva-bhūteṣu na me dveṣyaḥ asti na priyaḥ |
ye bhajanti tu mām bhaktyā mayi te teṣu ca api aham ||

sentences.l: Equal I [am] among-all-beings; not to-me [is any] hateful, not dear. Who worship, but, me with-devotion — in-me [are] they, and-them in, too, I.
sentences.i: I am the same toward all beings; none is hateful to me, and none is dear. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I too am in them.
sentences.n: A statement of divine impartiality (samaḥ ... sarva-bhūteṣu, 'equal among all beings') immediately qualified by an exception for devotion: those who worship bhaktyā, 'with devotion', enjoy a mutual indwelling (te mayi, mayi ca te, 'they in me, and I in them') not granted automatically to all — the same reciprocity promised at 4.11's ye yathā māṃ prapadyante. Sandhi: समोऽहं is samaḥ+aham (avagraha); द्वेष्योऽस्ति is dveṣyaḥ+asti (avagraha); चाप्यहम् packs ca+api (a+a→ā) + api+aham (i+a→y a-).

sentences.t:
अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक् ।
साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः ॥
sentences.tr:
api cet su-durācāraḥ bhajate mām ananya-bhāk |
sādhuḥ eva saḥ mantavyaḥ samyak vyavasitaḥ hi saḥ ||

morph.gloss: even
if (written joined before su-, no change)
very, exceedingly (intensifying prefix)
evil conduct, bad behavior (su-durācāra: 'of very evil conduct', nom. sg. masc., subject; -aḥ before bh- → -o)
to worship, revere, resort to (present middle 3rd sg.)
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me'; joined before a-, no change)
not other, exclusive, undivided (first compound member)
sharing in, devoted to, partaking of (ananya-bhāj: 'exclusively devoted', nom. sg. masc., agreeing with the subject)
good, virtuous, a saint (sādhuḥ: nom. sg., predicate; -uḥ + e- → -ur e-)
indeed
he (saḥ: nom. sg. masc.; visarga dropped before the consonant m-)
to think, consider (mantavya: gerundive 'to be considered, to be regarded', nom. sg. masc., predicate)
correctly, rightly (adverb; -k + v- → -g v-, voicing)
to resolve, determine (vyavasita: past participle 'resolved, determined', nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ before h- → -o)
for, indeed
he (saḥ: nom. sg. masc., subject)

sentences.l: Even if of-very-evil-conduct [one] worships me exclusively-devoted, a-saint indeed he [is] to-be-regarded — rightly he-has-resolved, for, he.
sentences.i: Even a person of very wicked conduct, if he worships me with undivided devotion, should be regarded as righteous, for he has made the right resolve.
sentences.n: One of the poem's boldest promises: even a su-durācāraḥ, 'one of very evil conduct' (su- here intensifying, not softening, the dur- 'bad'), becomes sādhuḥ, 'a saint', simply by worshiping Kṛṣṇa ananya-bhāk, 'with undivided devotion' — because the decisive thing is not his past conduct but that he has vyavasitaḥ, 'resolved', samyak, 'rightly'. Sandhi: सम्यग्व्यवसितो packs samyak+vyavasitaḥ (-k+v-→-g v-, voicing) with the whole compound's own visarga then falling before the voiced h- of hi (-aḥ before h-→-o); साधुरेव is sādhuḥ+eva (-uḥ+e-→-ur e-).

sentences.t:
क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति ।
कौन्तेय प्रति जानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति ॥
sentences.tr:
kṣipram bhavati dharma-ātmā śaśvat śāntim nigacchati |
kaunteya prati jānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati ||

morph.gloss: quickly, soon (adverb)
to become (present 3rd sg.)
dharma, kept untranslated (first compound member)
self, soul (dharma-ātman: 'whose soul/nature is dharma, dharma-souled', nom. sg. masc., predicate; a + ā → ā)
perpetual, everlasting (adjective/adverb; -t + ś- → -cch-, assimilation)
peace, tranquility (acc. sg. fem., object of nigacchati)
to attain, arrive at (present 3rd sg.)
'son of Kuntī', Arjuna (vocative)
to declare, affirm, promise, be assured of (compound verb, Monier-Williams; prati: the verbal prefix, not an independent adverb)
to declare, affirm (jānīhi: imperative 2nd sg., completing the compound verb begun by prati, 'declare with certainty!, be assured!')
not
I (me: gen. sg. enclitic 'my')
devotee (nom. sg., subject)
to perish, be destroyed (present 3rd sg.)

sentences.l: Quickly he-becomes dharma-souled, lasting peace he-attains; O son-of-Kuntī, know-for-certain: not my devotee perishes.
sentences.i: He quickly becomes a soul settled in dharma and attains lasting peace. Know for certain, Kaunteya, that my devotee never perishes.
sentences.n: The promise of verse 30 continues: the reformed devotee becomes dharma-ātmā, 'dharma-souled', kṣipram, 'quickly', and the teaching closes with Kṛṣṇa's flat guarantee, na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati, 'my devotee does not perish' — a line often quoted on its own. Sandhi: शश्वच्छान्तिं packs śaśvat+śāntim (-t+ś-→-cch-, assimilation), the first instance in this chapter of a dental stop assimilating fully to a following palatal.

sentences.t:
मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः ।
स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम् ॥
sentences.tr:
mām hi pārtha vyapāśritya ye api syuḥ pāpa-yonayaḥ |
striyaḥ vaiśyāḥ tathā śūdrāḥ te api yānti parām gatim ||

morph.gloss: I (acc. sg. 'me')
for, indeed
'son of Pṛthā', Arjuna (vocative)
to take refuge in, resort to (vyapāśritya: gerund 'having taken refuge in')
who (ye: nom. pl. masc. relative; ye + api: e + a → e with avagraha)
even
to be (syuḥ: optative 3rd pl. 'may be, though they be')
sinful, base, evil (first compound member)
womb, origin, source of birth (pāpa-yoni: 'of sinful, base origin', nom. pl. masc., predicate)
woman (striyaḥ: nom. pl. fem., in apposition; -aḥ before v- → -o)
a member of the vaiśya class, merchant or commoner (vaiśyāḥ: nom. pl., in apposition; -āḥ + t- → -ās t-)
likewise, and
a member of the śūdra class (śūdrāḥ: nom. pl., in apposition; -āḥ + t- → -ās t-)
they (te: nom. pl. masc., subject; te + api: e + a → e with avagraha)
too, also
to go, attain (present 3rd pl.)
highest, supreme (parām: acc. sg. fem., agreeing with gatim)
goal, destination (acc. sg., object of yānti)

sentences.l: Me, for, O son-of-Pṛthā, having-taken-refuge-in, who even might-be of-sinful-origin — women, vaiśyas, and śūdras as-well — they too attain the-supreme goal.
sentences.i: For those who take refuge in me, Pārtha, even if they are of low birth — women, merchants, or laborers — they too reach the highest goal.
sentences.n: The chapter's clearest statement of its universalism: pāpa-yonayaḥ, 'those of sinful/base origin' (a phrase describing low social status by birth, not moral fault), explicitly including striyaḥ, 'women', vaiśyāḥ, 'commoners', and śūdrāḥ, 'laborers' — the classes and sex excluded from direct Vedic study — nonetheless attain parāṃ gatim, 'the supreme goal', through nothing but taking refuge in Kṛṣṇa (mām vyapāśritya), a claim verse 33 intensifies by contrast. Sandhi: वैश्यास्तथा and शूद्रास्तेऽपि both show -āḥ+t-→-ās t-; स्त्रियो is striyaḥ, -aḥ before v-→-o.

sentences.t:
किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा ।
अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम् ॥
sentences.tr:
kim punar brāhmaṇāḥ puṇyāḥ bhaktāḥ rāja-ṛṣayaḥ tathā |
anityam asukham lokam imam prāpya bhajasva mām ||

again, moreover (retains -r before the voiced br-)
a brahmin, member of the priestly class (nom. pl., subject)
meritorious, holy, pure (nom. pl. masc., agreeing with brāhmaṇāḥ; visarga dropped before the voiced bh- of bhaktāḥ, the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ)
devoted, past participle of bhaj (nom. pl. masc., in apposition; visarga dropped before the voiced r- of rājarṣayaḥ, the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ)
king, royal (first compound member)
sage, seer (rāja-ṛṣi: 'royal sage', nom. pl. masc., in apposition; a + ṛ → ar)
likewise, and (rājarṣayaḥ + tathā: -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
impermanent, transient (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with lokam; joined before a-, no change)
unhappy, joyless, without ease (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with lokam)
world (acc. sg. masc., object of prāpya)
this (imam: acc. sg. masc., agreeing with lokam; joined, no change)
to attain, reach (gerund 'having attained')
to worship, revere, resort to (bhajasva: imperative middle 2nd sg. 'worship!')
I (acc. sg. 'me')

sentences.l: How-much-more, then, holy brahmins, devoted, royal-sages likewise! This impermanent, joyless world having-attained, worship me.
sentences.i: How much more, then, holy brahmins and devoted royal sages! Since you have come into this impermanent, joyless world, worship me.
sentences.n: An a fortiori argument from verse 32: if even those of low birth reach the highest goal through devotion, kiṃ punar, 'how much more' would brahmins and rāja-ṛṣayaḥ, 'royal sages' (a term recalling that this very teaching is itself rāja-vidyā, 'royal knowledge', from verse 2) — the verse then turns to direct exhortation, urging Arjuna (having attained this anityam asukham lokam, 'impermanent, joyless world') to worship Kṛṣṇa now. Sandhi: पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः retains -r before the voiced br- (like punar āvartinaḥ in 8.16); राजर्षयस्तथा packs rāja+ṛṣayaḥ (a+ṛ→ar) + rājarṣayaḥ+tathā (-aḥ+t-→-as t-).

sentences.t:
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।
मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः ॥
sentences.tr:
man-manāḥ bhava mad-bhaktaḥ mad-yājī mām namaskuru |
mām eva eṣyasi yuktvā evam ātmānam mat-parāyaṇaḥ ||

morph.gloss: me (stem form, first compound member)
mind (man-manas: 'whose mind is on me', man-manāḥ: nom. sg. masc., predicate; visarga dropped before the voiced bh- of bhava, the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ)
to be (bhava: imperative 2nd sg. 'be!')
me (stem form, first compound member)
devotee (mad-bhakta: 'my devotee', nom. sg. masc., predicate; -aḥ before m- → -o)
me (stem form, first compound member)
worshiper, sacrificer (mad-yājin: 'my worshiper', nom. sg. masc., predicate)
I (acc. sg. 'me')
homage, obeisance (first part of the compound verb namas-kṛ)
to do, make (kuru: imperative 2nd sg., namaskuru: 'bow down!, pay homage!')
I (mām: acc. sg. 'me'; joined before e-, no change)
indeed, surely (eva + eṣyasi: a + e → ai)
to go, come (eṣyasi: future 2nd sg. 'you shall come')
to join, discipline, unite (yuktvā: gerund 'having disciplined, having united'; yuktvā + evam: ā + e → ai)

self, soul (ātmānam: acc. sg., object of yuktvā)
me (stem form, first compound member)
the supreme goal, the highest resort (mat-parāyaṇa: 'intent on me, devoted to me as the highest goal', nom. sg. masc., predicate)

sentences.l: Mind-on-me become, my-devotee, my-worshiper, to-me bow-down; to-me-alone-indeed you-shall-come, having-thus-disciplined the-self, intent-on-me-as-the-highest-goal.
sentences.i: Fix your mind on me, become my devotee, my worshiper; bow down to me. Having thus disciplined yourself and made me your highest goal, you will come to me alone.
sentences.n: The chapter's closing exhortation, restating its whole teaching as four brief imperatives — man-manāḥ, 'mind on me', mad-bhaktaḥ, 'my devotee', mad-yājī, 'my worshiper', and namas-kuru, 'bow down' — before the final promise, mām eva eṣyasi, 'you shall come to me alone', for the one who is mat-parāyaṇaḥ, 'intent on me as the highest goal'. The same four-part formula recurs verbatim at 18.65, closing the poem's final teaching as well. Sandhi: मन्मना is man-manāḥ with its visarga dropped (not -o) before the voiced भ- of bhava, since the ending here is -āḥ, not -aḥ, as with several -āḥ forms earlier in this chapter; मद्भक्तो is mad-bhaktaḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o; मामेवैष्यसि packs mām+eva (joined) + eva+eṣyasi (a+e→ai); युक्त्वैवमात्मानं packs yuktvā+evam (ā+e→ai) + evam+ātmānam, joined.

glossary.श्रीभगवानुवाच: śrī-bhagavān uvāca — śrī — holy, glorious (honorific prefix); bhagavat — the Blessed One, the Lord — Kṛṣṇa's title as speaker (nom. sg. bhagavān; -n + u- written joined); vac — to speak (uvāca: perfect 3rd sg. 'said')
glossary.इदं: idam — idam — this (nom./acc. sg. neut., referring forward to jñānam of the second line)
glossary.ते: te — tvam — you (te: enclitic dat. sg. 'to you')
glossary.गुह्यतमं: guhyatamam — guhya-tama — most secret, superlative of guhya (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with idam)

glossary.यज्ज्ञात्वा: yat jñātvā — yad — which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, referring to jñānam; -t + j- → -j jñ-, assimilation); jñā — to know (jñātvā: gerund 'having known')
glossary.मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात्: mokṣyase aśubhāt — muc — to release, free (mokṣyase: future middle 2nd sg. 'you shall be released'; -e + a- → -e with avagraha); a-śubha — inauspicious, evil (aśubhāt: abl. sg. neut., 'from evil')
glossary.राजविद्या: rāja-vidyā — rāja — king, royal (first compound member); vidyā — knowledge, science (rāja-vidyā: 'royal knowledge, the king of sciences', nom. sg. fem., in apposition to the jñāna of verse 1)
glossary.राजगुह्यं: rāja-guhyam — rāja — king, royal (first compound member); guhya — secret (rāja-guhya: 'royal secret, the king of secrets', nom. sg. neut.)
glossary.पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम्: pavitram idam uttamam — pavitra — pure, purifying (nom. sg. neut.; joined before i-, no change); idam — this (nom. sg. neut., referring to the jñāna of verse 1; joined before u-, no change); uttama — highest, supreme (nom. sg. neut.)

glossary.धर्म्यं: dharmyam — dharmya — conformable to dharma, righteous (nom. sg. neut.)
glossary.सुसुखं: su-sukham — su — good, easy (prefix); sukha — ease, happiness (su-sukha: 'very easy', nom. sg. neut.)
glossary.कर्तुमव्ययम्: kartum avyayam — kṛ — to do, perform (kartum: infinitive 'to do, to practice', governed by sukham, 'easy to do'); a-vyaya — imperishable, undiminishing (nom. sg. neut.; joined before a-, no change)

glossary.मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि: mṛtyu-saṃsāra-vartmani — mṛtyu — death (first compound member); saṃsāra — transmigration, the cycle of rebirth (second member); vartman — path, road (mṛtyu-saṃsāra-vartman: 'the path of death and transmigration', loc. sg.)
glossary.ततमिदं: tatam idam — tan — to stretch, extend, pervade (tata: past participle 'pervaded, extended', nom. sg. neut.); idam — this (nom. sg. neut.; joined before i-, no change)

about: Chapter 9, Rājavidyārājaguhyayoga, "the royal knowledge, the royal secret," has Kṛṣṇa announce to Arjuna the most confidential teaching of the poem so far: knowledge joined with direct realization, easy to practice and imperishable. He opens with a paradox he spends the first third of the chapter working out — the whole world rests in him, pervaded by his unmanifest form, and yet he is not confined within it, as space contains the wind without being limited by it; nature (prakṛti) acts and unwinds the cosmos through endless cycles of creation and dissolution, but only under his oversight, so that he himself remains untouched, seated as if indifferent, by what it does. The deluded, he says, despise him for the human body he has taken on, missing his true nature as the great lord of beings and clinging instead to a demonic, self-defeating nature of their own, while the great-souled take refuge in his divine nature and worship him with undivided minds. Three dense catalog verses have him identify himself outright with every element of Vedic sacrifice and every name for ultimate reality — the rite, the offering, the fire, the mantra, the Vedas themselves, father, mother, a further twelve-name catalog of goal, sustainer, lord, witness, abode, refuge, friend and more, and finally being and non-being — before two four-line verses turn this into a pointed critique of ritualists who win only a temporary heaven and cycle back to mortal life once their merit runs out, unlike those who seek Kṛṣṇa himself and are freed for good. He promises to personally look after the welfare of those exclusively devoted to him, concedes that even worship of other deities, done with faith, ultimately reaches him (if not by the correct method), and lays out the simplest possible devotional practice: a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water, offered with devotion, accepted from anyone of disciplined mind, with the instruction to turn every action, every meal, every gift and every austerity into an offering to him. The chapter closes on its most radical promise, that even a person of thoroughly wicked conduct becomes a saint through undivided devotion, and that the supreme goal is open equally to women, merchants and laborers, and all the more so to the pious and the royal sages, if only they take refuge in him and make him their highest goal.
